title: Intermittent GPU RSS escalation observed during micro-batch streaming with pooled allocator
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: Production clusters running continuous micro-batching workloads intermittently show sustained GPU RSS increases over tens of minutes despite stable request rates and KV cache hit rates. Symptoms resemble delayed free/fragmentation interactions in the pooled allocator when combined with cudaMallocAsync's asynchronous release path and frequent small KV pin/unpin operations from chat sessions.

Observed behavior:
- RSS climbs by 6-12% over 30-90 minutes during mixed short/long sequence traffic, then partially recovers after maintenance window or node restart.
- cudaMallocAsync allocation count spikes aligned with micro-batch merges. Async free latency distributions show long tails (~200-800ms) on some streams.
- KV cache shows bursts of evictions followed by warm-up allocations; warm-up allocations often allocate many small chunks (~32-512B) that appear to land in dedicated tiny-slab pools.
- No obvious host OOMs; only GPU memory fragmentation and resident set growth.

Reproduction steps attempted (non-prod):
1) Replay production traces in perf-cluster using identical batching parameters (batch size distribution, merge window).
2) Run with allocator debug flags to log slab and pool metadata every minute.
3) Enable stream tracing for cudaMallocAsync and track deferred-free completion events.
4) Toggle KV cache prefetch (on/off) and observe allocator behavior.

Findings so far:
- When KV pin/unpin at high frequency interleave with continuous batching, small-chunk churn increases and tiny-chunk slab occupancy climbs without proportional large-chunk reclamation.
- Deferred-free callbacks are occasionally delayed by cross-stream synchronization, causing transient retention of slabs that prevent coalescing.
- The pooled allocator's heuristic for tiny-slab compaction doesn't trigger under heavy small-allocation churn, leaving many partially-filled slabs resident.
- Enabling a conservative tiny-slab compaction policy reduces RSS growth in repro by ~40% but increases short-term allocation latency and small-contention tail.

Impact hypothesis: A combination of deferred-free tail events (cudaMallocAsync) + tiny-slab contention from KV cache warm-ups leads to effective fragmentation that manifests as net RSS growth under continuous batching. This primarily affects customers with chat workloads that aggressively prefetch KV shards and use mixed sequence lengths.
comments: 2026-02-21 - Sofia Martinez: Opened ticket after noticing trend in perf-cluster; attached initial heap snapshots and allocation histograms.
2026-02-24 - Ethan Park: Ran repro with trace v2 and confirmed long-tailed deferred-free completions on stream GPU-3. Captured trace-id: trace-20260224-49.
2026-02-27 - Priya Desai (Infra): Observed that enabling tiny-slab compaction flag reduced steady RSS in repro. Suspect compaction threshold too high by default.
2026-03-02 - Sofia Martinez: Tried a targeted mitigation (limit concurrent KV prefetches to 4); RSS slope reduced but still present in mixed-traffic pattern.
2026-03-05 - Ethan Park: Drafted allocator change: add epoch-based deferred-free cap + opportunistic slab coalescer. Created draft PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/3678.
2026-03-09 - Performance Team: Ran load test with PR branch; median latency unchanged, p99 small-allocation latency increased by ~15ms. Memory growth eliminated in 6/6 runs.

2026-03-10 - Sofia Martinez: Decided to proceed with iterative approach: (1) ship telemetry/metrics to detect long-tail deferred frees in prod, (2) land opt-in allocator flags behind runtime toggle for canary, (3) follow with safer default changes after 1-week canary.
2026-03-10 - Ethan Park: Assigned follow-ups and will prepare rollout playbook including rollback criteria and observability dashboards.
2026-03-11 - QA: Will run regression suite focusing on small-allocation latency and KV cache hit curves for canary clusters.
proposed_fix: Phase 1 (canary): Add runtime flags to enable (a) epoch-based cap on outstanding deferred frees per-GPU-stream, (b) lowered tiny-slab compaction threshold under high tiny-churn, and (c) passive metric that emits deferred-free tail percentiles + slab occupancy per pool. Phase 2: If canary stable, integrate a background slab coalescer that runs when overall RSS approaches target headroom, and tune KV prefetcher to avoid simultaneous fan-out across all worker threads. Implementation will be gated and feature-flagged.
acceptance_criteria: Canary clusters with opt-in flags show no sustained RSS growth on replayed production traces across 72-hour runs
No regression in median per-request latency (>5% increase) on canary compared to baseline
Deferred-free tail p95/p99 metrics drop by at least 50% on canary
Operational runbook documented: how to enable/disable flags, rollback steps, and dashboards to monitor
